hints.title: Read the inequality as a picture
hints.body: The mean [f(a)+f(b)]2 is the height of the chord’s midpoint. The other side is the curve’s height at the same horizontal midpoint.
hints.recap: The chord’s midpoint must lie at or above the curve.
hints.pitfall: This compares shape, not the sign of the height.
hints.pause: Sketch the chord joining two points on an upward-opening parabola.

recall.reminder: Compare a chord’s position with the curve to read its bending.

hints.title: Distinguish vertical position from bending
hints.body: Explore what a vertical translation does to the given midpoint comparison; also compare left and right sides of an upward parabola.
hints.recap: Height, gradient and change of gradient are different properties.
hints.pitfall: A decreasing segment can still bend upward.
hints.pause: Determine which quantities the midpoint condition can constrain.

recall.reminder: Height, gradient and change of gradient are different properties.

hints.title: Test a local violation
hints.body: Suppose the relevant derivative sign condition fails on a small interval; sketch the chord and its midpoint relative to the curve there.
hints.recap: Necessity can be proved by showing failure would contradict the original condition.
hints.pitfall: The original inequality permits equality, so linear portions need checking.
hints.pause: Complete the local contradiction and express the resulting global non-strict condition.

recall.reminder: Necessity can be proved by showing failure would contradict the original condition.
New learning: the second derivative measures how the gradient changes. Compare tangent slopes as you move along a curve.

solution:
The point halfway along the chord from (a,f(a)) to (b,f(b)) has coordinates (a+b2,[f(a)+f(b)]2). The stated inequality says this chord midpoint is at least as high as the curve at the same input, for every interval.

If f″(x0)<0 somewhere, polynomial continuity makes f″ negative on a small interval around x0. There the graph bends downward, so its chord midpoint lies strictly below the curve midpoint. Taking a and b in that interval contradicts the required inequality. Therefore f″(x)≥0 for every real x.

The other options are not necessary. The upward-opening quadratic x2 satisfies the midpoint inequality, but its slope takes both signs and its height is not always nonpositive. The function x2−1 has the same bending but takes negative values, excluding a required nonnegative height. Also x2 has positive second derivative, excluding a required nonpositive second derivative.

Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Translate a midpoint chord inequality into nonnegative curvature
